lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if you could just describe a diagram in a chat, and have it drawn for you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That would save me a lot of fiddling with boxes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That was the idea behind D2COpenAIPlugin, an earlier ChatGPT plugin by Antoine. It generates diagrams with PlantUML or Mermaid straight from the conversation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's the difference between those two?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Both are text-based diagram languages. You write a few lines describing the boxes and arrows, and the tool draws the picture. The plugin lets ChatGPT write those lines and get back the rendered diagram.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So how does ChatGPT talk to it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The plugin is a small Python service built with FastAPI and run with uvicorn. ChatGPT calls its routes, and a manifest tells ChatGPT what the plugin can do. The repository has the details of the routes and setup.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. It sits on the path toward uml-mcp, Antoine's open-source M C P server for diagrams, which does the same job in Cursor and through a custom GPT.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The project page has a demo animation of it at work.
